key_insight: The paper introduces LabSafety Bench, a targeted benchmark that measures large language models' ability to detect hazards and assess risks in laboratory scenarios, revealing substantial variability and systematic failure modes across models.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of standardized, domain-specific evaluation for LLM safety in laboratory and experimental settings, enabling systematic measurement of models' hazard recognition and risk assessment capabilities before deployment.
method: Construct a curated suite of lab scenarios and questions covering hazard identification, mitigation suggestions, and risk-severity assessment.
Design task-specific metrics to score correctness, completeness, and conservativeness of model responses (e.g., hazard detection rate, mitigation quality, severity calibration).
Evaluate a range of popular LLMs under consistent prompting and reporting protocols to compare performance and surface common failure modes.
impact: Provides practitioners a practical tool to benchmark and compare LLM safety in experimental environments, guiding model selection, fine-tuning, and deployment safeguards to reduce real-world laboratory risk.
visual_elements: Bar chart comparing model scores across tasks (hazard ID, mitigation, severity calibration).
Pipeline diagram: scenario → prompt → LLM response → automated scoring → human review.
Heatmap or matrix showing common failure modes by model and hazard type (chemical, biological, electrical).
Risk-severity scale icon set (low → medium → high) with example model outputs annotated.
paper_title: Benchmarking large language models on safety risks in scientific laboratories
paper_authors: Yujun Zhou, Jingdong Yang, Yue Huang, Kehan Guo, Zoe Emory
